research_question.title: Family persistence of coordinate-compatible structured embeddings

curve_families: deterministically generated ordinary prime-order short-Weierstrass curves without special j-invariants
methods: coordinate-specific additive expansion and structured-density measurement

research_question.motivation: EXP-SGCP-EMBED-001 constructed a valid coordinate-compatible partial operation on one five-bit curve, but the valid order ideal lost substantial final support. A family experiment is needed to distinguish a fixture artifact from a persistent support-versus-composability tradeoff and to test whether actual coordinate predicates outperform symmetry-matched random x-fiber sets.
research_question.decision_target: Decide whether any preregistered coordinate predicate has a reproducible support-at-density advantage over matched random-x controls across curves and increasing toy sizes, or whether the valid embedding's support loss persists within the exact tested family.
constraints: The builder may use field coordinates, curve arithmetic, and public predicate parameters, but no scalar indices or discrete-log table.
Every factor base contains both signs over exactly B/2 selected non-2-torsion x-fibers; all controls match B and this negation symmetry.
Every reported embedding must satisfy the exact partial-monoid, compatibility, injectivity, acyclicity, source, and final-edge conditions inherited from EXP-SGCP-EMBED-001.
An optimizer row must report an exact primary optimum or a certified integer lower/upper support interval; unresolved rows cannot support a positive family claim.
Private optimizer state, final-support witnesses, and audit tables are charged and are not free structured advice.
No direct retained-4F by retained-4F edge may appear in the public partial operation.
Isogeny-transformed sets, relation matrices, target descent, and rho comparison are outside this experiment.
All results are TOY-EVIDENCE, MODEL-BOUND, and NOVELTY-UNVERIFIED.
